title: Starting a tenancy in the Northern Territory
description: Steps before and at the start of an NT tenancy. Summarised from NT Consumer Affairs guidance.

sources.title: A Guide to Renting in the Northern Territory
Pools or spas at rental properties

items.title: Advertise at a fixed rent: rent bidding is banned
Only ask applicants for the information NT Consumer Affairs approves
Sign a written tenancy agreement with the standard terms, at no cost to the tenant
Make sure approved photoelectric smoke alarms are fitted
If there's a pool or spa, have a compliance certificate or acknowledgement notice in your name (the NT pool compliance certificate application)
Make sure the home is clean, in reasonable repair, habitable and has adequate locks
Take a security deposit of no more than 4 weeks' rent and hold it in trust
items.detail: The NT has no bond authority. Agents use a tenancy trust account.

items.title: Give a receipt for the deposit and rent straight away (2 business days for transfers)
Give the ingoing condition report within 3 business days of the tenant moving in
Respond to the tenant's changes to the report within 5 business days
Keep copies of the agreement, condition report and receipts
